message.content:
**Quick‑start**

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T
```

That one line will force‑terminate *every* instance of **VS Code** (the `code.exe` process) and all of its child processes.

---

## What the switches mean

| Switch | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `/IM`  | Image name – the executable you want to kill (`code.exe`). |
| `/F`   | Force termination (no graceful shutdown). |
| `/T`   | Terminate the specified process **and** any child processes it spawned. |

If you only want to kill a specific instance, you can first find its PID:

```cmd
tasklist /FI "IMAGENAME eq code.exe"
```

Then kill that PID:

```cmd
taskkill /PID <pid> /F
```

---

## Alternative ways

| Method | Command | Notes |
|--------|---------|-------|
| **PowerShell** | `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` | Works from a PowerShell prompt; no need to specify `/T`. |
| **WMIC** | `wmic process where name="code.exe" delete` | Older but still works on many Windows versions. |
| **tskill** | `tskill code` | A quick shortcut, but less explicit than `taskkill`. |

---

## Filtering by user (optional)

If you’re on a multi‑user machine and only want to kill your own VS Code processes:

```cmd
taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq %USERNAME%"
```

Replace `%USERNAME%` with your actual login name if you prefer a literal string.

---

## Things to keep in mind

1. **Unsaved work** – `taskkill /F` will close VS Code immediately, so any unsaved files will be lost.  
2. **Admin rights** – You usually don’t need elevated privileges to kill your own processes, but if you’re targeting processes owned by another user or system processes, you’ll need to run the command prompt as Administrator.  
3. **Multiple instances** – VS Code can spawn several helper processes (`code.exe`, `code-helper.exe`, etc.). The `/T` switch ensures all of them are terminated.

---

### Quick cheat‑sheet

| Goal | Command |
|------|---------|
| Kill all VS Code processes (force) | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /T` |
| Kill a specific PID | `taskkill /PID <pid> /F` |
| Kill only your own VS Code | `taskkill /IM code.exe /F /FI "USERNAME eq %USERNAME%"` |
| PowerShell equivalent | `Stop-Process -Name code -Force` |

That’s it! Use the command that best fits your workflow.
